question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Ahuja is a cleverest lawyer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. clever.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The article "a" cannot be used with the superlative degree ("cleverest"). A superlative always takes "the" (the cleverest). Since the sentence uses "a", the adjective must be in the positive degree — "clever".

◦ Correct: Ahuja is a clever lawyer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "most clever" and Option 3 "cleverer" would also need a comparison ("the most clever", "cleverer than ..."), which is absent here.

• Option 4 "more clever" (comparative) requires "than" — no comparison exists in the sentence.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: clever – cleverer (with "than") – cleverest (with "the"). Rule: a/an + positive degree, the + superlative degree, comparative + than.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Curse
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Praise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Curse" means to use offensive words against someone; to wish evil or misfortune upon someone. (शाप देना / कोसना)

• Its antonym is "praise", which means to express approval or admiration of someone. (प्रशंसा करना)

◦ Example: Instead of cursing his rival, he began to praise his hard work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Criticise" (to point out faults) and Option 2 "Abuse" (to insult) are synonyms of curse, not antonyms.

• Option 4 "Comment" (to give an opinion) is neutral and unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of curse: abuse, damn, condemn, revile. Antonyms: praise, bless, commend, applaud.

question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

She always wears dresses of _________ fashion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the latest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The latest" means the most recent/newest. Dresses "of the latest fashion" = dresses of the newest style. The superlative "latest" must take the definite article "the". (नवीनतम)

◦ Correct: She always wears dresses of the latest fashion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "late" means delayed/dead (the late Mr Sharma) — it does not mean "newest" here.

• Option 2 "the latter" means the second of two things mentioned — no such pair exists.

• Option 3 "latest" without "the" is incomplete, as a superlative needs the article "the".

NOTE

• Distinguish: later/latest refer to time (the latest news), while latter/last refer to position/order (the latter half, the last chapter).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The discussion led by the scientist was very ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. informative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the intensifier "very", we use the positive degree of an adjective. "Informative" (giving useful information) fits perfectly. (ज्ञानवर्धक / जानकारीपूर्ण)

◦ Correct: The discussion led by the scientist was very informative.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "more informative" (comparative) needs "than"; Option 4 "most informative" (superlative) needs "the" and a group for comparison — "very" cannot precede either.

• Option 3 "information" is a noun; an adjective is required after "was very".

NOTE

• "Very + positive adjective" (very informative), "much + comparative" (much more informative), "by far + superlative" (by far the most informative).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Manisha had a great feeling for those who were junior than her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. junior to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Latin-origin comparative adjectives such as "junior, senior, superior, inferior, prior, anterior, posterior" take the preposition "to", NOT "than". So "junior to her" is correct.

◦ Correct: Manisha had a great feeling for those who were junior to her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "junior of" and 3 "junior from" use wrong prepositions.

• Option 4 is wrong because "junior than" is grammatically incorrect and needs substitution.

NOTE

• Remember for SSC exams: senior to, junior to, superior to, inferior to, preferable to, prior to — never "than" with these words.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Wolves’ teeth are larger and strong than dog’s teeth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. stronger.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" demands the comparative degree, and the adjective must stay parallel with "larger". Hence "larger and stronger than". (तुलनात्मक डिग्री)

◦ Correct: Wolves' teeth are larger and stronger than dog's teeth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "more strong" is unidiomatic — short adjectives form the comparative with "-er" (strong → stronger).

• Option 3 "the stronger" wrongly adds the article; Option 4 "strongest" is a superlative and cannot be used with "than".

NOTE

• Parallelism rule: adjectives joined by "and" must be in the same degree — "larger and stronger", "bigger and better". One-syllable adjectives take "-er/-est", not "more/most".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Native' from the given sentence.

Mr. Smith believes that various tribes are the indigenous habitants of various corners of the world; unlike his contemporaries who have a viewpoint regarding an alien or foreign invasion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Indigenous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Native" means belonging naturally to a place; originating in a particular region. Its closest synonym in the sentence is "indigenous" — occurring/living naturally in a region. (देशज / स्थानीय / मूल निवासी)

◦ Example: Tribes are the native/indigenous inhabitants of these regions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Foreign" (from another country) and Option 3 "Alien" (belonging to another place) are antonyms of native.

• Option 4 "Invasion" (an attack/entry by force) is a noun and unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of native: indigenous, aboriginal, local, domestic. Antonyms: foreign, alien, exotic, immigrant.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Anticipate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Predict.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anticipate" means to expect or foresee something before it happens. Its closest synonym is "predict" — to say what will happen in the future. (पूर्वानुमान करना / पहले से अपेक्षा करना)

◦ Example: The weather office anticipated/predicted heavy rain over the weekend.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Accuse" (to blame someone), Option 3 "doubt" (to be uncertain) and Option 4 "Conceal" (to hide) are unrelated to expecting something in advance.

NOTE

• Synonyms of anticipate: predict, expect, foresee, forecast, envisage. Antonym: doubt (in the sense of not expecting), be unaware of.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

A few students have condemned the latest project of preparing teaching aids as a waste of money.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Applauded.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Condemned" means expressed strong disapproval of; criticised severely. (निंदा की)

• Its antonym is "applauded" — praised or expressed approval (literally, clapped for). (सराहा / प्रशंसा की)

◦ Example: While a few students condemned the project, the teachers applauded it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Contradicted" (denied/opposed a statement) is closer to a synonym of disapproval.

• Option 2 "Doomed" (destined to fail) and Option 4 "Consolidated" (strengthened/combined) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of condemn: denounce, censure, criticise, deplore. Antonyms: applaud, praise, commend, approve.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Crocodile tears
option_2: To not behave in a fair way
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. An insincere display of grief.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "crocodile tears" means a false, insincere or hypocritical show of sorrow. (घड़ियाली आँसू — दिखावटी दुख)

◦ Example: She shed crocodile tears at the meeting, though she was secretly happy about her rival's failure.

• The idiom comes from the ancient belief that crocodiles weep while devouring their prey.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "An irrevocable step" matches "to cross the Rubicon".

• Option 2 "To not behave in a fair way" matches "to play foul / hit below the belt".

• Option 3 "To please everyone" matches "to run with the hare and hunt with the hounds".

NOTE

• Related idioms: "wear one's heart on one's sleeve" (show feelings openly), "put on an act" (pretend). "Crocodile tears" is a favourite SSC idiom — remember: fake sorrow.

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The magician performed a magnificant trick.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. magnificent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "magnificent", meaning extremely beautiful, grand or impressive. (भव्य / शानदार)

◦ Correct: The magician performed a magnificent trick.

• Spelling key: MAG + NI + FI + CENT (only one "i" before "-cent", no "a").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "magnificant", "magneficent", "magnificante" and "magnificient" are all misspellings — errors occur in the vowels ("a/e/i") before "-cent".

NOTE

• Similar "-cent" spellings often tested in SSC: magnificent, munificent (very generous), beneficent (doing good), reminiscent (reminding of). Related forms: magnificence (noun), magnificently (adverb).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Michael Jackson is known as the King of Pop. He ________ his own genre of music, Pop. His music is spreading its influence and popularity ________ the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. dominates; around.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dominates" means has a commanding position over; is the most important in. Michael Jackson dominates his own genre, Pop. The singular subject "He" needs the singular verb "dominates". (प्रभुत्व रखता है)

• "Around the world" is the correct fixed expression meaning all over the world. (दुनिया भर में)

◦ Correct: He dominates his own genre of music ... popularity around the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "command" does not agree with "He" (it should be "commands"), and "besides" (in addition to) is wrong.

• Option 3 "beside" means "next to" — incorrect here.

• Option 4 "presides" needs "over" (presides over), and "round the world" is less appropriate in this context.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: singular subject → verb + s/es. Fixed phrases: "around the world", "all over the world", "across the globe".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A blue-eyed boy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. one who is favourite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a blue-eyed boy" means a person who is someone's favourite; one who is highly favoured and given special treatment (especially by a person in authority). (चहेता / कृपापात्र व्यक्ति)

◦ Example: Rohan is the blue-eyed boy of the manager, so he gets all the important projects.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "an unperceived observer" matches "a fly on the wall".

• Option 2 "a miser" matches "a penny-pincher".

• Option 3 "an unwelcome intruder" matches "a gatecrasher".

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "the apple of one's eye" (someone very dear), "teacher's pet" (a teacher's favourite student). In American English, the phrase is "fair-haired boy".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Ceased' to fill in the blank.

He was _______ from his job because of his misconduct.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. terminated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ceased" means stopped; brought to an end. Its synonym "terminated" means ended/dismissed. "He was terminated from his job" = his job was brought to an end (he was dismissed). (समाप्त किया गया / नौकरी से हटाया गया)

◦ Correct: He was terminated from his job because of his misconduct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "continued" (kept going) and Option 4 "progressed" (moved forward) are antonyms of ceased.

• Option 3 "commenced" means began — also opposite in sense.

NOTE

• Synonyms of cease/terminate: stop, end, discontinue, halt, conclude. Antonyms: commence, begin, continue, start.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to complete the given sentence in the present perfect continuous tense.

The company ___________________ working towards achievements in curbing slackness and fostering development.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. has been.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The present perfect continuous tense = has/have + been + verb-ing. "The company" is a singular subject, so it takes "has been working". (पूर्ण वर्तमान सतत काल)

◦ Correct: The company has been working towards achievements in curbing slackness and fostering development.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "have been" is used with plural subjects (They have been working).

• Options 2 "are being" and 3 "is being" form the present continuous passive, not the present perfect continuous.

NOTE

• Tense structures for SSC: Present perfect continuous — has/have been + V-ing (since/for); Past perfect continuous — had been + V-ing. Collective nouns like "company", "team", "committee" normally take a singular verb.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The sharpshooter _________ dead a man-eating tiger after it allegedly killed nine people in the last few days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. shot.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct collocation is "shot dead" — to kill by firing a gun. A sharpshooter (an expert marksman) shot dead the man-eating tiger. (गोली मारकर मार डाला)

◦ Correct: The sharpshooter shot dead a man-eating tiger ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fixed dead" and Option 2 "threw dead" are not valid English collocations.

• Option 4 "killed dead" is redundant — "killed" already means caused death.

NOTE

• "Shoot – shot – shot" (V1–V2–V3). Common collocations: "shot dead", "shot at", "gunned down". The word "sharpshooter" itself hints at shooting.

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error in the given sentence.

The reorganisation of daily life wrought by industrialisation had effects that weakened the material basis for the instietutions of the family and the community.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. institutions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "institutions" — established organisations, customs or systems in a society (here, the family and the community as social institutions). (संस्थाएँ)

◦ Correct: ... weakened the material basis for the institutions of the family and the community.

• Spelling key: IN + STI + TU + TIONS.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "instietutions" (given in the sentence), "instetusion", "instetuitions" and "instetutions" are all misspellings — the correct form has "insti-", not "inste-", and no extra "i".

NOTE

• Related words: institute (verb/noun), institution (noun), institutional (adjective). Do not confuse with "intuition" (instinctive understanding).

question:
The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

He missed the college bus / because he woke up / unpardonably lately in the morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. unpardonably lately in the morning.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is in the word "lately". "Lately" means recently/of late — it does NOT mean "not on time". The correct adverb here is "late" (after the proper time). So the segment should be "unpardonably late in the morning".

◦ Correct: He missed the college bus because he woke up unpardonably late in the morning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "He missed the college bus" and "because he woke up" are grammatically correct segments.

NOTE

• Confusing adverb pairs for SSC: late (after the due time — He came late) vs lately (recently — He has been ill lately); hard (with effort) vs hardly (scarcely); near (close) vs nearly (almost).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted word(s) in the given sentence.

The sceneries in Darjeeling are breathtaking.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. scenery in Darjeeling is.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Scenery" is an uncountable noun — it has no plural form ("sceneries" is incorrect) and takes a singular verb. Hence "The scenery in Darjeeling is breathtaking".

◦ Correct: The scenery in Darjeeling is breathtaking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 2 and 3 retain the incorrect plural "sceneries".

• Option 1 uses "scenery" correctly but pairs it with the plural past verb "were", which is wrong for a singular uncountable noun in a present-tense statement.

NOTE

• Uncountable nouns that never take "-s" and always take a singular verb: scenery, furniture, information, advice, luggage, machinery, poetry, news. To count them, use "a piece of scenery/furniture/information".

question:
One of the four words in bold in the given sentence is incorrectly spelt. Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

The detectives uncovered a conspirasy to overthrow the government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. conspirasy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Conspirasy" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "conspiracy" — a secret plan by a group to do something unlawful or harmful. (षड्यंत्र / साज़िश)

◦ Correct: The detectives uncovered a conspiracy to overthrow the government.

• Spelling key: CON + SPI + RA + CY (ends in "-cy", not "-sy").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "detectives" (investigators), "uncovered" (discovered/exposed) and "overthrow" (to remove from power by force) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: conspire (verb), conspirator (person), conspiratorial (adjective). Words ending in "-cy": conspiracy, democracy, accuracy, legacy, fallacy.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Worldwide illiteracy rates have (1)_________ declined in the last few decades. One of the major reasons for this decline is the sharp increase in literacy rates (2)_________ young women, which is a result of specific (3)_________ designed to increase educational opportunities for girls. (4)_________, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world, about two-thirds of whom are (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. consistently.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Consistently" means steadily; in the same way over a period of time without change. Illiteracy rates have "consistently declined in the last few decades" — i.e., they have fallen steadily and continuously. (लगातार / निरंतर)

◦ Correct: Worldwide illiteracy rates have consistently declined in the last few decades.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "thirdly" (in the third place) needs a list of points — none exists here.

• Option 2 "wearily" (tiredly) is illogical for statistics.

• Option 3 "consequently" (as a result) shows a result, but no cause has been stated yet — the decline is being described, not caused.

NOTE

• "Consistently" (steadily, uniformly) vs "constantly" (all the time) vs "consequently" (therefore). Adverbs of manner like "consistently" typically sit between the auxiliary and the main verb: have consistently declined.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Worldwide illiteracy rates have (1)_________ declined in the last few decades. One of the major reasons for this decline is the sharp increase in literacy rates (2)_________ young women, which is a result of specific (3)_________ designed to increase educational opportunities for girls. (4)_________, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world, about two-thirds of whom are (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. among.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Among" is used for more than two people or a group considered collectively. "Literacy rates among young women" = literacy rates within the group of young women. (के बीच — समूह के लिए)

◦ Correct: ... the sharp increase in literacy rates among young women ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "between" is used for two persons/things (between two friends), not for a large group.

• Option 2 "over" (above) and Option 4 "against" (in opposition to) do not fit the sense of "within a group".

NOTE

• Preposition rule for SSC: "between" = two; "among" = more than two/a group. E.g., "Divide the sweets between the two boys but among the five girls".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Worldwide illiteracy rates have (1)_________ declined in the last few decades. One of the major reasons for this decline is the sharp increase in literacy rates (2)_________ young women, which is a result of specific (3)_________ designed to increase educational opportunities for girls. (4)_________, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world, about two-thirds of whom are (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. campaigns.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Campaigns" means organised courses of action/planned activities intended to achieve a particular goal (here, increasing educational opportunities for girls). (अभियान)

◦ Correct: ... which is a result of specific campaigns designed to increase educational opportunities for girls.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "companions" (friends/associates), Option 3 "camisole" (a woman's undergarment) and Option 4 "champions" (winners/supporters) make no sense with "designed to increase educational opportunities".

NOTE

• "Campaign" collocates with: launch/run/lead a campaign, awareness campaign, literacy campaign, election campaign. In India, "Beti Bachao Beti Padhao" is a well-known campaign for girls' education.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Worldwide illiteracy rates have (1)_________ declined in the last few decades. One of the major reasons for this decline is the sharp increase in literacy rates (2)_________ young women, which is a result of specific (3)_________ designed to increase educational opportunities for girls. (4)_________, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world, about two-thirds of whom are (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. However.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "However" shows contrast between two statements. The passage first says illiteracy has declined; then, in contrast, "However, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults". (फिर भी / तथापि)

◦ Correct: However, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Whenever" (at any time when) introduces a time clause — no time reference exists.

• Option 2 "Otherwise" (if not/or else) shows a condition — not intended here.

• Option 3 "Thus" (therefore) shows a result, but the sentence contradicts, not follows from, the earlier one.

NOTE

• Contrast connectors: however, nevertheless, nonetheless, yet, still, on the other hand. They are usually followed by a comma at the start of a sentence.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Worldwide illiteracy rates have (1)_________ declined in the last few decades. One of the major reasons for this decline is the sharp increase in literacy rates (2)_________ young women, which is a result of specific (3)_________ designed to increase educational opportunities for girls. (4)_________, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world, about two-thirds of whom are (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. women.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "about two-thirds of whom" refers to 771 million illiterate adults — a plural group — so the plural noun "women" is required. The passage is about literacy among young women, so the contrast is that most illiterate adults are still women. (महिलाएँ)

◦ Correct: ... about two-thirds of whom are women.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "man" and 2 "woman" are singular and cannot follow the plural verb "are" for two-thirds of 771 million adults.

• Option 3 "child" is singular and also illogical — the passage talks about illiterate adults.

NOTE

• Irregular plurals: man → men, woman → women, child → children. As per UNESCO data, nearly two-thirds of the world's illiterate adults are women — a common fact in SSC comprehension passages.

question: Which red and buff sandstone is the tallest tower in India built in the thirteenth century?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Qutub Minar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Qutub Minar in Delhi, built of red and buff sandstone, is the tallest tower (minaret) in India, completed in the early thirteenth century. (क़ुतुब मीनार — भारत की सबसे ऊँची मीनार)

• Its construction was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak (founder of the Slave/Mamluk dynasty) around 1199 and completed by his successor Iltutmish; it is about 72.5 metres (238 feet) high with five storeys.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Qutub Minar was built to celebrate Muslim rule in Delhi and is dedicated to the Sufi saint Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1993).

• The Qutub complex also houses the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, the rust-free Iron Pillar of Chandragupta II's period and the Alai Darwaza (built by Alauddin Khalji).

NOTE

• Shaheed Minar is in Kolkata; Chand Minar is at Daulatabad (Maharashtra); Jhulta Minar (shaking minarets) is in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.

question: The people of Himachal Pradesh make channels to bring water from a glacier or rainwater to villages for the function of mainly irrigation. These channels are locally known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guls or Kuls.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Western Himalayas (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir), people build diversion channels called "Guls or Kuls" to carry water from glaciers/streams to their villages, mainly for irrigation of fields. (गुल या कुल — हिमाचल की सिंचाई नहरें)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Khadins — earthen embankments for harvesting rainwater in the farmland of Jaisalmer, Rajasthan (also called dhora).

• Johads — small earthen check dams/storage pits of Rajasthan used to conserve rainwater.

• Baori/Baoli — stepwells used for storing drinking water, common in Rajasthan and other parts of north-western India.

NOTE

• Traditional water-harvesting systems (NCERT): Kuls/Guls (Himalayas), Khadins and Johads (Rajasthan), Bandharas/Tals (Maharashtra), Bundhis (MP/UP), Ahars-Pynes (Bihar), Kattas (Karnataka), Eris (tanks, Tamil Nadu), Surangams (Kerala), Zings (Ladakh).

question: In which year was the microfinance movement formally launched in India on a pilot basis?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1992.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The microfinance movement was formally launched in India on a pilot basis in 1992, when NABARD started the Self-Help Group–Bank Linkage Programme (SHG-BLP), linking informal women's self-help groups with banks for small loans. (सूक्ष्म वित्त — 1992, नाबार्ड की एसएचजी-बैंक लिंकेज योजना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Microfinance means providing small loans (micro-credit), savings and insurance services to poor households who lack access to formal banking.

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) was set up in 1982 on the recommendation of the Shivaraman Committee.

• The model was inspired by the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh, founded by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus.

NOTE

• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme is today the world's largest microfinance programme; SHGs typically consist of 10–20 members, mostly women.

question: Who among the following founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara, called Nagalapuram, after his mother?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Krishna Deva Raya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Krishna Deva Raya (r. 1509–1529), the greatest ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire (Tuluva dynasty), founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara called "Nagalapuram", named after his mother Nagala Devi. (कृष्णदेव राय — नागलापुरम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Krishna Deva Raya wrote the Telugu work "Amuktamalyada" (on statecraft) and the Sanskrit play "Jambavati Kalyanam"; his court had the Ashtadiggajas (eight great Telugu poets), including Tenali Ramakrishna.

• He was known as "Andhra Bhoja" and "Abhinava Bhoja" and maintained friendly relations with the Portuguese (traveller Domingo Paes visited his court and praised his rule).

• The ruins of Vijayanagara at Hampi (Karnataka) are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Vijayanagara dynasties in order: Sangama → Saluva → Tuluva → Aravidu. Sadasiva Raya and Rama Raya were associated with the period of the Battle of Talikota (1565), which ruined Vijayanagara.

question: In which sport is the term 'Dolphin Kick' commonly used?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swimming.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The term "Dolphin Kick" is used in swimming. It is the leg movement in which both legs kick together in a wave-like (undulating) motion, like a dolphin's tail — chiefly used in the butterfly stroke and in underwater phases after starts and turns. (डॉल्फ़िन किक — तैराकी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Main swimming strokes: freestyle (front crawl), backstroke, breaststroke and butterfly.

• Swimming terms: lap, flip turn, medley, relay, dolphin kick, streamline. The world body for aquatics is World Aquatics (formerly FINA), headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

NOTE

• Sports terms often asked in SSC: Javelin Throw/Long Jump/High Jump are athletics field events (terms: run-up, take-off, foul line), while "dolphin kick", "butterfly", "freestyle" belong to swimming.

question: Which of the following novels is based on Malgudi, a fictional town in south India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Guide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Guide" (1958) is a famous novel by R. K. Narayan set in "Malgudi", the fictional south Indian town he created for most of his works. (द गाइड — आर. के. नारायण, मालगुडी)

• The novel won the Sahitya Akademi Award (1960) — R. K. Narayan was the first Indian English writer to receive it — and was made into the popular film "Guide" (1965) starring Dev Anand.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "My Days" is R. K. Narayan's autobiography, not a Malgudi novel.

• "A Suitable Boy" is by Vikram Seth; "Sacred Games" is by Vikram Chandra — neither is set in Malgudi.

• Other Malgudi works: Swami and Friends, The Bachelor of Arts, The English Teacher, Malgudi Days.

NOTE

• R. K. Narayan received the Padma Bhushan (1964) and Padma Vibhushan (2000) and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha. "Malgudi Days" was made into a much-loved TV series.

question: In which of the following years did India NOT win an Olympic gold medal in hockey?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1960.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India did NOT win the hockey gold at the 1960 Rome Olympics — India lost the final 0–1 to Pakistan and won the silver medal, ending India's streak of six consecutive golds (1928–1956). (1960 रोम ओलंपिक — भारत को रजत पदक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India's eight Olympic hockey golds: 1928 (Amsterdam), 1932 (Los Angeles), 1936 (Berlin), 1948 (London), 1952 (Helsinki), 1956 (Melbourne), 1964 (Tokyo) and 1980 (Moscow).

• 1948 London gold was India's first as an independent nation; Balbir Singh Sr. starred in 1948–56, while Major Dhyan Chand ("the Wizard of Hockey") led the 1928–36 era.

NOTE

• India also won hockey bronze medals in 1968, 1972, 2020 (Tokyo) and 2024 (Paris). National Sports Day (29 August) marks Dhyan Chand's birthday.

question: Which of the following states is characterised by salt marshes known as 'Rann'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The salt marshes known as "Rann" are found in Gujarat — the Great Rann of Kutch and the Little Rann of Kutch in the Kachchh district. These are vast, seasonally flooded salt flats/marshes. (कच्छ का रण — गुजरात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Rann of Kutch is famous for the Rann Utsav (a cultural festival on the white salt desert) and is the only home of the Indian Wild Ass (Ghudkhar) — protected in the Wild Ass Sanctuary, Little Rann.

• The Kutch region also hosts flamingo breeding grounds (Flamingo City) and the Harappan site of Dholavira (UNESCO World Heritage Site).

NOTE

• During the monsoon, the Rann floods with saline water; in the dry season it becomes a white encrusted salt desert. The 1965 India–Pakistan conflict also involved the Rann of Kutch boundary.

question: Who among the following wrote a book called ‘Indica’ based on his travels and experiences in Mauryan India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Megasthenes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Megasthenes" was the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus I Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra. He wrote the famous account "Indica", describing the society, administration and cities of Mauryan India. (मेगस्थनीज — इंडिका)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The original Indica is lost; it survives in fragments quoted by later Greek writers such as Strabo, Diodorus, Arrian and Pliny.

• Megasthenes described Pataliputra's municipal administration (six committees of five members each) and divided Indian society into seven classes.

• Other sources on the Mauryas: Kautilya's Arthashastra, Vishakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa, and Ashokan edicts.

NOTE

• Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus Nicator (c. 305 BCE); the treaty gave the Mauryas territories of eastern Afghanistan/Balochistan, and Seleucus received 500 war elephants.

question: In which of the following states is the Jawara dance performed on the occasion of a successful harvest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Jawara" is a harvest folk dance of the Bundelkhand region of Madhya Pradesh, performed to celebrate a successful harvest. Women dance carrying baskets full of jawara (young wheat/barley shoots) balanced on their heads. (जवारा नृत्य — मध्य प्रदेश, बुंदेलखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Madhya Pradesh: Matki, Phulpati, Grida, Maanch, Tertali, Gaur (Bastar region borders).

• Harvest dances of other states: Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Dhamal/Phag (Haryana), Garba/Dandiya Raas (Gujarat — Navratri), Bihu (Assam), Karma (Jharkhand/MP).

NOTE

• In SSC exams, folk dance–state pairs are frequently asked; remember Jawara, Matki and Maanch for Madhya Pradesh.

question: Who among the following was a leader of Garam Dal, a group of radical nationalists?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bipin Chandra Pal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Garam Dal" (the Extremist/radical wing of the Indian National Congress) was led by the famous trio "Lal–Bal–Pal" — Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal. Hence Bipin Chandra Pal was a Garam Dal leader. (गरम दल — लाल-बाल-पाल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Surendranath Banerjee were leaders of the Naram Dal (Moderates), who believed in petitions, prayers and constitutional methods.

• The Extremists believed in Swaraj, Swadeshi, boycott and national education; they rose to prominence during the anti-partition (of Bengal) Swadeshi Movement, 1905.

• The Congress split into Moderates and Extremists at the Surat Session, 1907; the two wings reunited at the Lucknow Session, 1916.

NOTE

• Tilak's famous declaration: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it." Bipin Chandra Pal is called the "Father of Revolutionary Thoughts" in India.

question: Who among the following presides over the meeting of the Council of Ministers in a state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chief Minister of the state.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Chief Minister" is the head of the state Council of Ministers and presides over its meetings. He/she is the real executive head of the state government, just as the Prime Minister is at the Centre. (मुख्यमंत्री — राज्य मंत्रिपरिषद की बैठकों की अध्यक्षता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 163 — Council of Ministers with the CM at its head to aid and advise the Governor; Article 164 — the CM is appointed by the Governor, other ministers on the CM's advice.

• The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly (Article 164(2)); ministers' strength cannot exceed 15% of the Assembly's strength (91st Amendment, 2003).

• The Chief Secretary heads the state's civil services; the Speaker presides over the Legislative Assembly; the Chairman presides over the Legislative Council.

NOTE

• The Governor is the nominal (constitutional) head of the state, while the Chief Minister is the real executive — mirroring the President–Prime Minister relationship at the Centre (Articles 74, 75).

question: Which of the following is NOT a function of mesosomes?
option_1: Increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content
option_4: DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells
solution_text:
The correct answer is Locomotion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mesosomes" are infoldings (extensions) of the plasma membrane in bacterial (prokaryotic) cells. Locomotion is NOT their function — movement in bacteria is carried out by flagella. (मीसोसोम — गति इनका कार्य नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Functions of mesosomes (NCERT Class 11, Cell: The Unit of Life):

◦ Help in cell wall formation,

◦ DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells,

◦ Respiration and secretion,

◦ Increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and its enzymatic content.

• Mesosomes occur as vesicles, tubules and lamellae.

NOTE

• Bacterial structures for movement: flagella (locomotion); pili and fimbriae are surface structures that help in attachment/conjugation, not motility. Mesosomes are sometimes called "chondrioids" as they perform respiration like mitochondria.

question: Who was sworn in as the Governor of Chhattisgarh in February 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Biswabhusan Harichandan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 2023, "Biswabhusan Harichandan" was sworn in as the Governor of Chhattisgarh. He was earlier the Governor of Andhra Pradesh (2019–2023). (विश्वभूषण हरिचंदन — छत्तीसगढ़ के राज्यपाल, फरवरी 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He succeeded Anusuiya Uikey, who was transferred as the Governor of Manipur in the same reshuffle.

• Biswabhusan Harichandan is a veteran politician and writer from Odisha, honoured with the Kalinga Ratna award.

• The Governor is appointed by the President under Article 155 and holds office during the President's pleasure (Article 156); minimum age is 35 years (Article 157).

NOTE

• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000; its capital is Raipur (Nava Raipur Atal Nagar) and its High Court is at Bilaspur — the state was in the news for the same February 2023 gubernatorial reshuffle.

question: Which of the following Khayal artists is the founding father of Lalit Kala Kendra of the University of Pune?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhimsen Joshi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, the legendary Khayal (Hindustani classical) vocalist of the Kirana gharana, is regarded as the founding father of the Lalit Kala Kendra (Centre for Performing Arts) of the University of Pune (Savitribai Phule Pune University). (पं. भीमसेन जोशी — ललित कला केंद्र, पुणे विश्वविद्यालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bhimsen Joshi received the Bharat Ratna in 2008 (the first Hindustani vocalist to get it); he founded the famous Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Mahotsav in Pune in memory of his guru Sawai Gandharva.

• He is renowned for his khayal singing and devotional music (abhangs, bhajans) and featured in the national integration song "Mile Sur Mera Tumhara".

NOTE

• The other options: Ravi Shankar — sitar maestro; Shiv Kumar Sharma — santoor maestro; Kishan Maharaj — tabla maestro (Banaras gharana) — none of them is a Khayal vocalist.

question: Which of the following is NOT a hydroelectric power plant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sambhar Lake Hydel Project.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sambhar Lake" in Rajasthan is India's largest inland SALT lake — it is used for salt production, and there is no hydroelectric project on it. Hence "Sambhar Lake Hydel Project" is NOT a hydroelectric power plant. (सांभर झील — खारे पानी की झील, कोई जलविद्युत परियोजना नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bhakra Nangal Project — on the Sutlej river (Himachal Pradesh/Punjab); the Bhakra dam (Gobind Sagar reservoir) is one of the highest gravity dams in India.

• Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC, 1948) — multipurpose project on the Damodar river (Jharkhand/West Bengal), modelled on the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) of the USA.

• Kopili Hydel Project — on the Kopili river in Assam (NEEPCO), in the north-east.

NOTE

• Sambhar Lake is a Ramsar wetland near Jaipur, famous for flamingoes and salt harvesting. Hydel power needs flowing/falling water, which a shallow salt lake cannot provide.

question: Which of the following is an alarming effect of thermal pollution in water bodies?
option_1: The amount of dissolved oxygen decreased significantly
option_3: The random changes in pH values
solution_text:
The correct answer is The amount of dissolved oxygen decreased significantly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Thermal pollution" is the rise in the temperature of water bodies, mainly caused by the discharge of hot water from thermal power plants and industries. Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen (DO) — so the most alarming effect is that the amount of dissolved oxygen decreases significantly, harming fish and aquatic life. (तापीय प्रदूषण — घुलित ऑक्सीजन में कमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lower dissolved oxygen suffocates fish and other aquatic organisms, raises their metabolic rate and makes them more vulnerable to disease; a sudden temperature change ("thermal shock") can even kill fish.

• The solubility of gases (including O₂) in water decreases as temperature rises.

• Changes in turbidity, pH and CO₂ levels may occur, but the sharp fall in dissolved oxygen is the most alarming and characteristic effect of thermal pollution.

• Healthy water usually needs DO of about 6.5–8 mg/L; BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) is the indicator of organic pollution in water.

NOTE

• Main sources of thermal pollution: coolant water from thermal and nuclear power stations, steel mills and refineries. Cooling towers and cooling ponds are used to reduce it.

question: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 (A Progress Review), what was the proportion of population in multidimensional poverty (Headcount Ratio) in rural India in 2019-2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 19.28%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the "National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023: A Progress Review" released by NITI Aayog, the proportion of the population in multidimensional poverty (Headcount Ratio) in rural India in 2019–2021 was "19.28%" (down from 32.59% in 2015-16). (राष्ट्रीय बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2023 — ग्रामीण भारत 19.28%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In urban India, the headcount ratio fell from 8.65% to 5.27%; at the all-India level it declined from 24.85% (2015-16) to 14.96% (2019-21) — about 13.5 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21.

• The index is based on the NFHS surveys and uses three dimensions — health, education and standard of living — with 12 indicators (the global MPI of UNDP-OPHI uses 10).

NOTE

• The global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is published by the UNDP with the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI). In NITI Aayog's report, Bihar, Jharkhand and Meghalaya had among the highest poverty ratios.

question: According to Census 2011 of India, which metropolitan city has the highest population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, "Mumbai (Greater Mumbai)" is the metropolitan city with the highest population — about 1.84 crore (18.4 million) in the urban agglomeration and about 1.24 crore in the municipal area, making it India's most populous city. (मुंबई — 2011 की जनगणना में सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या वाला महानगर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rank of urban agglomerations (Census 2011): 1. Greater Mumbai, 2. Delhi, 3. Kolkata, 4. Chennai, 5. Bengaluru, 6. Hyderabad.

• Census 2011 was the 15th census of India (7th after Independence); its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future"; Census Commissioner — C. Chandramauli.

• India's population (2011): 121.09 crore; literacy rate 74.04%; sex ratio 943; density 382 persons/sq km; most populous state — Uttar Pradesh.

NOTE

• A city with a population of more than 10 lakh (1 million) is a "million-plus/metropolitan" city — there were 53 such cities in Census 2011; megacities (over 10 million): Greater Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata.

question: An Ummathat folk dancer from Karnataka ________ had been honoured with Padma Shri in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rani Machaiah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rani Machaiah" of Kodagu (Coorg), Karnataka, was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2023 (Art category) for her contribution to "Ummathat", the traditional folk dance of the Kodava community, performed by women. (रानी मचैया — उम्मथाट लोक नृत्य, पद्म श्री 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ummathat is performed by Kodava women in traditional attire, moving in a circle with brass cymbals, usually on festive occasions and in praise of the river goddess Kaveri.

• Rani Machaiah is popularly called the "Ummathat queen" and worked for decades to popularise Kodava folk culture.

NOTE

• The other options: Rani Karnaa — famous Kathak dancer; Devika Rani — the "First Lady of Indian cinema", first Dadasaheb Phalke Award winner (1969); Sharan Rani Backliwal — renowned sarod player. Padma awards are announced on Republic Day eve each year.

question: Who among the following was the founder of 'Bhoodan Yajna' in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vinoba Bhave.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bhoodan Yajna (Land-Gift Movement)" was founded by Acharya Vinoba Bhave in 1951, starting from Pochampally village (Telangana), where Ramachandra Reddy donated 100 acres of land. Under it, landowners were persuaded to voluntarily donate land to landless farmers. (भूदान आंदोलन — विनोबा भावे, 1951)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The movement later grew into "Gramdan" (donation of whole villages), beginning with Mangroth village (UP) and spreading widely in Odisha.

• Vinoba Bhave was chosen by Gandhiji as the first Satyagrahi of the Individual Satyagraha (1940); he founded the Sarvodaya movement and was the first recipient of the Ramon Magsaysay Award (1958); he received the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1983.

• He is called the "Acharya" and regarded as the spiritual heir of Mahatma Gandhi.

NOTE

• Pochampally, the birthplace of Bhoodan, is also famous for its Ikat (Pochampally) silk sarees and was named among UNWTO's "Best Tourism Villages".

question: Which part of a flower develops into a seed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ovule.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After fertilisation, the "ovule" of a flower develops into the seed, while the ovary develops into the fruit. (बीजांड — बीज में विकसित होता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Parts of a flower:

◦ Stamen — male reproductive part (anther + filament); the anther produces pollen grains.

◦ Pistil/Carpel — female reproductive part (stigma + style + ovary); the ovary contains ovules.

◦ Petals (corolla) — colourful parts that attract pollinators; sepals (calyx) — green parts that protect the bud.

• Fertilisation is the fusion of the male gamete (from pollen) with the egg cell inside the ovule; angiosperms show double fertilisation.

NOTE

• Remember for SSC: Ovary → Fruit; Ovule → Seed. The transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is pollination (by wind, water, insects, etc.).

question: In December 2023, which eminent agricultural economist from Kerala was conferred the distinguished title of ISAE Fellow 2023 by the Indian Society of Agricultural Economics (ISAE)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. P Indira Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In December 2023, "Dr. P. Indira Devi", an eminent agricultural economist from Kerala (former Director of Research, Kerala Agricultural University), was conferred the distinguished title of "ISAE Fellow 2023" by the Indian Society of Agricultural Economics (ISAE). (डॉ. पी. इंदिरा देवी — ISAE फेलो 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The award recognised her outstanding contribution to research and policy in agricultural economics — including work on pesticide-use behaviour, environmental economics and farm labour.

• The ISAE (founded 1939, Mumbai) is a premier professional body that promotes the study of agricultural economics and rural development in India.

NOTE

• The other options: Chanda Nimbkar — animal husbandry scientist; Dr. Suman Sahai — geneticist, founder of the "Gene Campaign"; Sulochana Gadgil — noted monsoon meteorologist/climate scientist.

question:
Which Article of the Indian Constitution states the following?

‘Directive Principles of State Policy are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the state to apply these principles in making laws.’
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 37.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Article 37" of the Constitution declares that the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country, and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws. (अनुच्छेद 37 — राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व शासन में मूलभूत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• DPSP are contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution and were borrowed from the Irish Constitution (Ireland, in turn, took them from Spain).

• Article 40 — organisation of village panchayats; Article 30 — right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions (a Fundamental Right); Article 35 — power of Parliament to make laws on certain Fundamental Rights.

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called DPSP the "novel features" of the Constitution; Granville Austin described DPSP and Fundamental Rights as the "Conscience of the Constitution".

NOTE

• Key DPSPs for exams: Art. 39A (equal justice, free legal aid), Art. 44 (Uniform Civil Code), Art. 45 (early childhood care), Art. 48 (agriculture/animal husbandry), Art. 50 (separation of judiciary from executive), Art. 51 (international peace).

question: Madhavpur Fair in Gujarat is a _______ day long event to celebrate Lord Krishna's marriage with Rukmani.
solution_text:
The correct answer is five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Madhavpur Fair (Madhavpur Ghed Mela)" of Gujarat is a "five-day" long fair that celebrates the marriage of Lord Krishna (Madhavrai) with Rukmini. It begins on Ram Navami (Chaitra month) at Madhavpur Ghed village, Porbandar district, near the Madhavrai temple. (माधवपुर मेला — पाँच दिवसीय, कृष्ण-रुक्मिणी विवाह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• During the fair, a colourful wedding procession of Lord Madhavrai is taken out and the marriage rituals are re-enacted for five days.

• As Rukmini is believed to be from Arunachal Pradesh (north-east) in the Mishmi tradition, the fair is promoted as a symbol of "Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat", connecting western and north-eastern India, with participation of artists from the north-eastern states.

NOTE

• Famous fairs of Gujarat: Madhavpur Mela, Tarnetar fair (Surendranagar), Vautha Mela and the Rann Utsav (Kutch). Fairs and festivals with their states are a recurring SSC GK topic.
